summary: Bug-fix verification round for Volumes step + backend regression on suggest-assumptions 'source' field. All 7 requested behaviours PASS. Volumes step relabelling (Typical units sold per month + labelled pattern row) works: flat/growth/rampup/q4/summer patterns correctly fill 12 month cells with expected shapes accounting for start-month offset (start=Sep-26: Q4 boost lands on Oct/Nov/Dec calendar months at table positions 1-3, summer boost on May-Aug at positions 8-11). Empty base + existing volumes reuses first non-zero value (55) and back-fills base box. Empty base + all-zero cells shows amber ring (border-amber-400 ring-2 ring-amber-200) on volume-base input and toast 'Type a typical monthly volume in the box first, then pick a pattern'. Clear button zeroes all 12 cells and empties base. Copy-from-above duplicates previous item's growth curve exactly. Individual cell edits propagate: item0 flat=10 with cell0 edited to 20 (110 units), item1 flat=5 (60 units), Costs (5/20) -> Review shows $6,660 revenue, $1,850 costs, $4,810 gross profit, 72.2% margin — arithmetic exact. Backend: added assertion for 'source' string field on /api/ai/suggest-assumptions — passes. All 4 pytest tests green in 20s.

issues: Pre-existing hydration warning: '<span> cannot be a child of <option>' from dev-time source-code instrumentation on profile-months select. Cosmetic, unchanged from iteration 1.

critical_code_review_comments: StepVolumes.jsx fill() correctly falls back to first non-zero existing unit via Array.prototype.find (num(u) > 0), sets base state to the resolved value, and clears the amber highlight on next base-input change — clean UX recovery.

applyPattern startIdx offset is derived from state.startMonth (parseInt of the MM part - 1) so calendar-based patterns (q4/summer) correctly follow the header labels rather than the raw table position.
Backend AssumptionResponse.source is Optional[str]; prompt instructs the LLM to return a named benchmark (never invent URL). LLM returns non-empty source in tests.
Minor: fill() overwrites any prior manual edits when reusing 'existing' base — acceptable since the button label ('fill all 12 months') telegraphs this.
